title: ValidationRule
description: A single input-validation constraint (regex pattern, numeric range, length limit, allowed-value list or custom check) that the value of a protected field or request attribute must satisfy, with a violation message and severity. It accepts or rejects the value itself and does not decide who may access it. Use AccessCondition instead when the predicate tests a request-context attribute (user, role, time, IP) to decide whether the request is authorized, rather than checking that a supplied value is well-formed. Use FieldAccessControl instead when the concern is how a field's value is masked, redacted or hidden from unauthorized principals, rather than which values are acceptable. Use PolicyRule instead when the unit produces a permit/deny decision with optional obligations, rather than a pass/fail check with a violation message. Use PasswordPolicy instead when the constraints are the complete credential complexity, rotation and lockout regime, rather than one individual check that such a policy might use.

type.description: Validation mechanism type, per NIST SI-10 (Information Input Validation).

value.description: Validation constraint value whose meaning depends on `type`: a regex pattern string, a numeric range expression (e.g. '1-100'), a maximum character count, a pipe-delimited list of allowed enum values, or a custom expression string.

message.description: Human-readable violation message shown to the user or logged when this validation rule fails.

severity.description: Severity of a validation rule violation.

x-dr-standard: NIST SP 800-53 SI-10 Information Input Validation
x-dr-evidence: Bean Validation, Pydantic, Joi or Zod constraints such as @Pattern, @Size, constr(regex=...) or .max() declared on security-sensitive DTO fields like email, account number, token or redirect URL.
Input-sanitization middleware or allowlist regexes that reject a request with HTTP 400/422 and a specific error message when a parameter fails the check.

A validator function or schema entry named for the check (e.g. validateIban, SAFE_FILENAME_RE) referenced from an access-control or field-protection layer, with configurable severity or logging on failure.
